stream_log.reasoning: Week of 2026-07-27 to 08-03. The fragile Jul 25-26 pause in the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis collapsed rather than consummated into a ceasefire. Fighting re-escalated all week: Saudi Arabia joined US strikes on Iran-backed proxies (Jul 28), Iran fired a ballistic-missile attack on US forces (intercepted, Jul 29) prompting Trump to say it was 'our turn' as the US completed a fresh round of strikes, and Trump escalated coercion by vowing to bomb one Iranian bridge or power plant for every ship fired on in Hormuz - i.e. deliberate targeting of Iranian civilian infrastructure. The naval blockade held and Houthi/Red Sea attacks continued. This drives middle_east_stability 0.14->0.13 (war widened with Saudi direct involvement and civilian-infrastructure targeting) and reverses last week's tentative de-escalation on nuclear_risk_level 0.34->0.35 (pause broke, Iran struck US bases, Trump threats resumed). Notably the economic transmission eased even as the war intensified: Brent came off its ~$97-100 peak to ~$88 (still +~20% on the month) and equities rallied on strong megacap earnings (S&P 500 +1.1%, Nasdaq +1.6% on the week; Microsoft and Amazon jumped, though Apple -7.4% and Meta fell), so global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks back up 1.00->1.01 as the acute oil-shock drag partially unwound. Russia-Ukraine ground on with Ukraine's deep-strike campaign degrading Russian energy infrastructure further (drones hit ~13 more energy facilities Aug 2, causing local blackouts), sustaining fuel-shortage pressure on Moscow: russia_stability 0.27->0.26, and two-front high-intensity combat (US-Iran with Saudi involvement, daily Ukraine-Russia exchanges, Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,512,500->1,516,000. Excluded/watched: China's gray-zone squeeze on Taiwan intensified (China Coast Guard containment-rehearsal patrols east of Taiwan, a Jul 20 CCG clash injuring a Philippine sailor near Second Thomas Shoal, PLA drone-warfare training in Russia) but is an incremental campaign already partly reflected, with no discrete single-week trigger; the frontier-AI wave continued (Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Kimi K3 at 2.8T params) but Google delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro and no event warrants another integer ai_development_year_offset tick weeks after the 4->5 move; seasonal monsoon flooding (Pakistan, Assam India ~5.6M affected) and European wildfires are regionally severe but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude. No new nodes: the re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node - a signed ceasefire, which did not materialize, would have warranted one.

Week of 2026-08-03 to 08-10. For the first time since the June ceasefire collapsed, the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis produced a substantive diplomatic framework rather than another failed pause: Iran and Oman announced agreement on a proposed shipping route (Aug 5-7) with a joint Tehran-Muscat statement in final drafting, Iran's FM Araghchi called a deal 'very close,' and Trump/Treasury Sec Bessent signaled a reopening 'soon.' Markets priced the de-escalation in hard - Brent fell more than 7% on the week (~$83-86) and the S&P 500 hit a record close Friday in its strongest week since April. This drives middle_east_stability 0.13->0.15 (framework deal emerging, though still subject to unmet conditions - Iran demands US compensation, troop withdrawal, war-end, and 5-7% transit fees, and a Houthi tanker strike still hit a Saudi vessel Aug 5), nuclear_risk_level 0.35->0.33 (positive/constructive talks reverse the prior re-escalation), supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.47 (partial reopening close, oil easing) and global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.01->1.02 (acute oil-shock drag unwinding further as equities rallied to records). Russia-Ukraine ground on at record intensity - Russia set a wartime record of 381 missiles in July (~12/day), glide-bombed Zaporizhzhia (Aug 2) and continued deep strikes - while the US Senate passed a sweeping Russia sanctions package 86-11, adding fresh structural pressure even as Russian territorial gains slowed (13 sq mi in four weeks vs 31 prior): russia_stability 0.26->0.25. Sustained but de-escalating two-front combat lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,516,000->1,519,000. Excluded/watched: no new node - the emerging Hormuz deal was not signed this week (still in drafting, subject to conditions), so this remains a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node; a consummated ceasefire next week would warrant one. Also excluded: China's gray-zone squeeze on Taiwan continued (Aug 1 CCTV amphibious-assault footage, Taiwan-Strait live-fire drills, Taiwan's annual war games and a new $25B defense package) but is an incremental campaign with no discrete single-week trigger; the frontier-AI wave stayed incremental (ByteDance Seedance 2.5 Aug 8, Meta Muse Glimmer Aug 10) after late-July flagships (Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.6 Flash) already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; severe US wildfires (Spokane Complex ~60k evacuated, Oregon 2M+ acres, ~250k acres across Washington) and continuing South Asian monsoon flooding are regionally acute but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-08-10 to 08-17. Russia-Ukraine produced a rare, publicized Ukrainian battlefield reversal: Kyiv completed its eight-month Oleksandrivka-axis counteroffensive (Jan 29-Aug 12), retaking ~745 sq km and 26 settlements and clearing Russia from nearly all of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast (~10,000 Russian troops killed per Zelenskyy), even as Russia intensified nightly combined strikes (12+ killed Aug 10-11, KN-23 North Korean missiles battle-tested) - this, plus the fresh 86-11 US Senate sanctions package and the Kremlin barring the anti-war Yabloko party from the September Duma elections, nudges russia_stability 0.25->0.24. On the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iran and Oman formalized a shipping-route agreement (announced Aug 15), the clearest de-escalation milestone since the June ceasefire collapsed - lifting middle_east_stability 0.15->0.16 and easing nuclear_risk_level 0.33->0.32 - but full reopening still hinges on the US lifting its blockade and sanctions (Araghchi: the Oman deal 'wouldn't translate into the strait's reopening'), and ship attacks continued, so the moves stay small and this remains a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node rather than a new one. Macro turned benign-to-positive: the S&P 500 hit records (clearing 7,800 for a third straight weekly gain) on softer-than-expected July CPI/PPI and an expected Fed hold, shrugging off Brent's climb to ~$87, so global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 1.02->1.03. Colombia's magnitude-7.4 quake (Aug 10) - its strongest this century, 132+ dead and rising with heavy damage in Pereira - drags latin_america_stability 0.40->0.38. Sustained high-intensity Ukraine combat (the culminating Dnipropetrovsk fighting and continued deep strikes) plus residual Gulf/Red Sea attacks lift cumulative conflict_deaths 1,519,000->1,522,000. Excluded/watched: no new node - the Iran-Oman deal is not a consummated US-Iran ceasefire (blockade holds) and Ukraine's gains are an operational success within the ongoing 2022_russia_ukraine war, not an era-defining discrete event; frontier-AI releases stayed incremental (Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; China-Taiwan pressure held roughly stable with no discrete single-week trigger; supply_chain_resilience held at 0.47 because the Hormuz strait did not actually reopen and oil ticked up on a large US crude stockpile build; and Cyclone Dolphin (China, 1M+ evacuated), Philippines/Sri Lanka monsoon flooding, Canadian (BC) wildfires and the ongoing DRC Ebola PHEIC were regionally acute but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-08-17 to 08-24. Last week's Hormuz optimism collapsed: the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding expired Aug 17 and Trump ruled out extending the ceasefire, declared no talks were underway (Aug 18), threatened to 'bomb the shit out of' Oman if it obstructed reopening the strait, and posted a 'New US Territory' image claiming 'total control' of Hormuz, while a senior Iranian official said Tehran would shift to a 'fully offensive' posture and mount a 'timely and precise' attack to break the US naval blockade (a carrier group was en route to replace USS Lincoln; the UAE detected a missile threat Aug 18). The Iran-Oman shipping framework announced last week did NOT translate into any reopening - Iran's preconditions (lift the blockade, withdraw US forces, permanently end the war) remain unmet and the blockade held all week. Markets re-priced the escalation: Brent surged ~6% to ~$94 (a second straight ~6% weekly gain, fully reversing the prior week's -7% relief rally), Houthis struck another Saudi vessel in the Red Sea, and Israel ramped up strikes on Lebanon and hit the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria. This reverses last week's tentative improvements: middle_east_stability 0.16->0.14 (deal collapsed, MOU expired, offensive threats, Lebanon/Syria widening - though Pezeshkian's Aug 21 signal that Tehran wants the war to end soon keeps the slip contained), nuclear_risk_level 0.32->0.34 (MOU lapse, 'fully offensive' threat, carrier surge and UAE missile scare), and supply_chain_resilience 0.47->0.45 (Brent back to ~$94, strait firmly not reopening, blockade entrenched). Macro turned mildly risk-off: the S&P 500 fell ~1.4% on the week to ~2% below its record as the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped ~5% on rising Treasury yields, Fed-independence worries ahead of Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address, and the renewed oil bid - so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.03->1.02, partially unwinding last week's tick. Russia-Ukraine ground on at high tempo (mutual missile/drone barrages killing civilians; Russian strikes have damaged 300+ Ukrainian fuel stations over six months) with only limited diplomacy - Moscow said it is 'ready for new ideas' but only ones matching Putin's existing goals - so two-front combat lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,522,000->1,525,000 while russia_stability holds at 0.24 (the grind and the tentative Russian openness roughly offset, no decisive single-week mover). Excluded/watched: no new node - the Hormuz re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a discrete era-defining event; Trump's 'very positive' outreach to Kim Jong-un and the scaled-down US-South Korea exercises are a minor Korea de-escalation with no clean structural dimension and are offset by the Iran nuclear-risk move; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna updates, Claude Sonnet 5 pricing made permanent, Grok Imagine Image 2.0, Meta Muse Spark) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; and the Indonesia M7.7 Flores earthquake (~70 dead) and record Japan/South Korea rainfall predate this window (Aug 13-14) and map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-08-24 to 08-31. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis cooled from an acute military standoff into an economic/sanctions confrontation: the US has not struck Iranian targets since late July and Trump canceled a planned attack citing progress in ceasefire negotiations, Iran's and Oman's foreign ministers met Aug 25 to firm up the shipping-corridor understanding, and crude flows through Hormuz recovered to ~6-8M bbl/day, so Brent fell ~5% on the week to ~$89-90 (from ~$94). This eases middle_east_stability 0.14->0.15, nuclear_risk_level 0.34->0.33, and supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.47 - moves kept small because the blockade nominally holds, Iran still calls the strait 'closed' with its preconditions unmet, and tankers were still hit this week (the LNG carrier Gaslog Shanghai and another vessel near Oman). Markets recovered on the oil relief and a strong Nvidia earnings beat (S&P 500 back to ~7,731, Nasdaq +1.6% on the day, PMI 51.0 still expansionary), lifting global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.02->1.03 and partially unwinding last week's risk-off tick. Russia-Ukraine ran at record intensity: Zelensky said Russia fired ~2,000 attack drones, 1,600+ glide bombs and 31 missiles (including North Korean ballistic) in one week, an Aug 29 strike on a warehouse west of Kyiv killed 38 with several missing, and Russia's MoD signaled a renewed winter energy-infrastructure campaign - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,525,000->1,529,000. Ukraine's deep-strike campaign escalated onto Russia's export economy - drone attacks suspended all three major grain terminals at Novorossiysk (cutting August Russian grain exports by an estimated 0.7-1.2M tonnes, potentially below 2M vs 5.7M a year ago) alongside a Leningrad Oblast oil refinery and a Krasnodar airbase - nudging russia_stability 0.24->0.23. That Black Sea disruption, atop Northern-Hemisphere drought that cut European wheat an estimated 8-10M tonnes, drove wheat +12% on the week to its highest since Feb 2023 (+54% YTD, with corn also at multi-year highs), so food_security_index eases 0.72->0.71 - the first genuine structural food-supply signal in the stream. Excluded/watched: no new node - the Hormuz de-escalation is a shift within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a signed ceasefire or discrete era-defining event, and the grain shock is a development within the ongoing 2022_russia_ukraine war; the US-Venezuela oil-access framework and a Dominican Republic-Venezuela diplomatic thaw are geopolitically notable but not a clean structural mover on latin_america_stability this week; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (Alibaba Qwen 3.8-Max at 2.4T params, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna, Meta Muse Spark, plus a first AI-piloted F-16 test flight) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; and South Korea's record 42.5C heat maps to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.
